title: Scheduled jobs — eleven crons and loops
why: Eleven rows the sweep found in the scheduler that name no capability because they *are* the capability's trigger, not the capability. The split the rows draw is retired versus not retired: reviews, lead_alerts, dual_role_guard, god_watch and all three `webhook_server.py` loops are classed LEGACY / UNREACHABLE, while reactivation (10:00 MSK), referral resolver (11:30), subscriptions (12:00) and loyalty (12:30) are NOT RETIRED and stay registered. Those four are FENCED on their rows — no row records any of the eleven emitting a client message directly, and where a row names an outcome at all it is one of the 12 canonical moments bound by G7, so on the rows' own account the cron is only a tick and authority stays server-side. One caveat travels with the split and cannot be detached from it: the split is drawn from a single evidence checkout, and the copy of `bot.py` on the branch this signature is being prepared from does not match that checkout — there the same seven bodies are live. The god_watch row is the sharpest case: it records a registration comment still claiming «MAYA сама проверяет систему и оплаты» against a body returning `retired_no_canonical_operational_occurrence`, and calls the behaviour authoritative; in the working-tree copy comment and behaviour agree, and the digest is built and sent. Recording the split, and recording that the two copies disagree about it — not deleting anything — is the whole of the group.
disappear: Nothing in Wave 1. Seven rows — the four retired crons and all three loops — carry retirementCondition «RETIRE IN K16 after the probe is recorded», and each one's parity requirement is a recorded unreachability probe, not an assumption. That probe is the load-bearing gate here rather than a formality: it is what has to settle the disagreement between the two copies before any of the seven is touched. The other four are OUT OF SCOPE WITH EXACT REASON and are not scheduled for removal at all.
remain: The four not-retired crons stay registered on their schedules, fenced as above; nothing about them changes in this wave. The seven retired registrations also stay in the code until K16. On the evidence rows the tick still fires while the body returns a retirement status — client_retention_refresh_loop and maya_operating_rhythm_loop are still spawned, reputation_monitor_loop is not spawned at all — while in the working-tree copy all three loops are spawned; that difference is part of what the probe must resolve. No successor is proposed for any of the eleven, and no row names a canonical owner: all eleven owner cells are what this signature supplies.
risk: MEDIUM — and not only as a record, for two reasons. First, the K16 cleanup is an AUTHORITY ratchet change, not a UX tidy-up: five of the seven retired rows are frozen by named AST guard contracts (package5_wave_rc_guard_contracts.py 'r06'/'r08', package5_operational_work_runtime_guard.py:61, package5_review_source_guard.py:32), S-783 is additionally covered by test_package5_b34_review_retirement.py, and S-773 and S-781 require a negative test on removal — every deletion costs a guard or test change. Second, the retired verdict is contradicted in hand, not merely unmeasured. In the copy of «ai администратор/bot.py» and «webhook_server.py» on the branch this dossier is being prepared from, all seven are live: `_reviews_job` dispatches review requests, `_god_watch_job` builds and sends the founder a system-and-payments digest over Telegram and PWA push, `_dual_role_guard_job` repairs and signals, `lead_alerts.scan_and_alert` alerts admins, and all three loops are spawned. The AST guards prove the retirement over the evidence checkout's source; they do not prove it over what is running. So this entry does not tell the owner that the 09:00 god_watch tick has stopped monitoring — it tells him two copies disagree and no one has yet probed the deployed VPS instance, which is not directly reachable from the work machine and has to be reached through the Beget jump host. That probe is exactly what all seven rows already demand. The level stays MEDIUM because this wave removes nothing and every removal is separately gated on that probe; it becomes HIGH the moment a K16 deletion is proposed on the strength of the snapshot alone, or the owner is advised to stop treating the 09:00 digest as monitoring.
user_impact: No user notices anything in Wave 1 — server-side attribution group, no UI, no primary-nav entry, "WHAT DISAPPEARS: nothing". But the group's premise must be corrected before it is signed. The dossier says reactivation, referral, subscriptions and loyalty "run daily against real clients" and rates the group MEDIUM because "four of these send messages to real clients on a schedule"; the proposed impact inherits that and says clients keep getting referral promo-code issuance (S-769) and loyalty earn/expiry (S-771) "on the same timers". At the verified code, that is false. All eleven rows still tick and none produces a client-, staff-, admin- or owner-visible effect: S-766 reactivation (10:00) and S-770 subscriptions (12:00) delegate to reactivation.py:173-176 / subscriptions.py:278-281, which return canonical_retention_entry.retention_owner_required(...) — {"status":"not_executed","error":"B35_CANONICAL_OWNER_REQUIRED","sent":0} from a module that by its own docstring "performs no IO and never resolves an audience" (the dossier rationale quotes the bot.py docstring, not the delegated body — same comment-vs-behaviour trap it flags for god_watch); S-769 referral (11:30) returns _legacy_referral_mutation_disabled("resolve_and_issue_referral_rewards") at referral.py:211-228 with pending/granted/expired all 0, so no promo code reaches anyone; S-771 loyalty (12:30) returns _legacy_loyalty_mutation_disabled("legacy_loyalty_daily_batch") at loyalty.py:553-555, which RAISES LegacyLoyaltyCutoverError (loyalty.py:68-71) and is swallowed by bot.py:4782-4788 as "Ошибка loyalty job" — a daily logged error, not a silent no-op — and run_earning_job (loyalty.py:395-402) and run_expiry_job (:488-498) are disabled the same way, so no points are earned and none expire on any path, cron or owner-panel. The owner-expectation problem is therefore not two stale promises but nearly the whole table: registration comments still promise «выдаём промокоды обоим участникам» (referral), push «продлить?» (subscriptions), «начисление + сгорание баллов» (loyalty), «рассылка созревших pending-запросов» (reviews S-772, _reviews_job → messages:0), «алерт о зависшей заявке» (lead_alerts S-773, scan_and_alert → retired_unverified_lead_occurrence) and «MAYA сама проверяет систему и оплаты» (god_watch S-776, → retired_no_canonical_operational_occurrence). In every case comment and behaviour disagree and the behaviour is authoritative. The owner should stop counting on the entire scheduled retention/loyalty/referral/review/alert story, not just the morning digest and lead alerts. This is not "the scheduler is dead": what still reaches people on a timer sits outside these eleven rows — the birthday cron (birthday.run_birthday_job has a real consent-gated body and is explicitly content-hash-excluded from retirement in package5_retention_runtime_guard.py) and the 11:00 cycle-reminder owner queue. Clients and staff see no difference in Wave 1 because there is nothing left here to differ. The MEDIUM risk rating should be re-based: there is no daily client-messaging traffic in this group to protect, and the actual risk of the record is that a later reader believes there is.
security_impact: NONE as a change in Wave 1 — nothing is removed or re-pointed, no client-side check is involved, and all eleven rows are schedulers with no surface. Four corrections to the authority framing. (1) The re-point already happened, before this wave. These are not dormant registrations but module-level refusals pending a canonical owner: canonical_retention_entry returns B35_CANONICAL_OWNER_REQUIRED with requires_review:true and instructs the owner to confirm audience and text in the MAYA panel; referral and loyalty return/raise p4_04 / p4_03 legacy-mutation-disabled. That is a standing authority decision — a schedule may not send a campaign; only a reviewed, owner-approved one may. The successor it names is owner approval in the panel, which is role-gated and therefore squarely inside the frozen "approval role-gated, NOT separation-of-duties" limitation; this group does not change that and must not be read as a control. (2) "A schedule is not an actor" survives, but scope it: S-774's status string is retired_identity_alert_not_authority and S-782's body comment is «R04: scheduling does not supply a canonical command or actor», so no row IN THIS GROUP records an authority check a server-side check would have to replace. Do not generalise to "no cron ever carried one". (3) The ratchet count is understated: eight of eleven are frozen by named contracts, not five — r06 in package5_wave_rc_guard_contracts.py pins _god_watch_job (S-776), _dual_role_guard_job (S-774) AND lead_alerts.scan_and_alert (S-773); r08 pins _reviews_job (S-772); package5_operational_work_runtime_guard.py:61 asserts maya_operating_rhythm_loop contains no ast.Call (S-782); package5_review_source_guard.py:32 pins reputation_monitor_loop → "return None" with test_package5_b34_review_retirement.py (S-783); package5_retention_runtime_guard.py (PRODUCERS + SCHEDULED) plus test_package5_wave_rb_r07.py pin reactivation and subscriptions (S-766, S-770). K16 retirement is an AUTHORITY ratchet change with negative tests across four guard modules — stronger than the record claims. (4) The unfrozen three are the real finding and point the opposite way from "no authority concern here": S-769 referral, S-771 loyalty and S-781 client_retention_refresh_loop have NO guard or negative test. Referral and loyalty are disabled only by a one-line early `return` standing in front of fully intact legacy bodies (referral.py:229ff and loyalty.py:557ff are unreachable dead code, not deleted), so deleting one line silently re-arms daily client-affecting mutations — promo-code issuance, point accrual and expiry — with no ratchet to catch it. That belongs in the record as a latent re-arm risk. Finally, the compensating-control sentence is half wrong and should not be carried as written: scheduled IDENTITY alerting is indeed absent (dual_role_guard is the only one and it is dead), but scheduled OPERATIONAL alerting is not absent — r06 re-pointed those paths to canonical_operational_alerts.trigger(), and live callers outside this group still fire it, including waitlist_admin_alert_loop (spawned at webhook_server.py:10162, every 120 s) plus record create/update/delete and shift reminders. The honest caveat is quality, not existence: trigger() is a trigger-only POST to http://127.0.0.1:3107/api/internal/legacy/operational-alerts/tick carrying no audience or content, and it returns False silently when MAYA_LEGACY_APPOINTMENT_BRIDGE_TOKEN is absent/short or the POST fails, on the stated principle that a lost trigger "neither proves delivery nor permits a provider retry". So the gap to record is: no scheduled identity alerting at all, and operational alerting delegated to an env-token bridge whose failure is unobservable from the Python side. Pre-existing; this group neither creates nor closes it.
